claims.text: The extent of chemically induced short-range order is the primary factor governing phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Increasing short-range order stabilizes a single-phase, potentially FCC, microstructure.
A stabilized single-phase microstructure underpins high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Reducing local chemical and strain heterogeneities suppresses deleterious phase transformations.
Conventional arc melting generally produces Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys with nearly random atomic distributions and low inherent short-range order.
Thermal treatments or minor compositional changes can increase short-range order without introducing new phases.
Enhanced short-range order produces greater local uniformity in atomic bonding.
Enhanced short-range order reduces lattice-strain concentrations.
Greater bonding uniformity and lower lattice-strain concentrations reduce the number of sites available for secondary-phase nucleation under thermal, irradiation, or cryogenic stresses.
Suppressing secondary-phase nucleation maintains the desired single-phase structure and its targeted mechanical and environmental properties.
Samples with enhanced short-range order will retain the desired phase better during high-temperature exposure, irradiation, and cryogenic cycling than low-SRO baseline samples.
Samples with enhanced short-range order will retain mechanical stability better than low-SRO baseline samples under the specified extreme conditions.
Baseline samples with minimal short-range order are more prone to phase separation or unwanted transformations.
Standard-processed Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni samples typically have lower phase stability under extreme conditions.
The proposed relationship is limited to Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys processed by routes that permit modulation of short-range order.
Applicability of the hypothesis to other alloy systems or processing routes is unverified.
The quantitative relationship between short-range-order magnitude and phase-stability improvement is not established.
The optimal amount of short-range order for balancing all targeted properties is uncertain.
